status_summary: No enacted law, bill or federal contracting rule imposing a citizenship share on contractor workforces was found. H.R. 9063, the Hire American Act, introduced 2026-05-29, would amend Title 5 to require that federal employees be U.S. citizens or nationals, with limited exceptions; per its GovInfo listing and trade press, it covers federal employment, not contractor workforces, and it is not counted as this recommendation. No bill amending the law to let private employers prefer citizens in hiring was found.
title: Require 70 percent U.S. citizens among workers on new federal contracts
uncertainties: Absence-of-evidence finding from two WebSearches (one by the researcher, one in review on contractor citizenship bills) and fetches of the GovInfo bill page, whose text was not available, and of a trade-press summary of H.R. 9063. The GovInfo listing cites 8 U.S.C. 1324b among its references, so the bill may touch the citizenship discrimination provision for federal employment; its text was not read. A first-term executive order on federal contractor use of foreign labor appeared in results and predates the window. A bill could exist that the searches missed; congress.gov could not be fetched. A federal acquisition rule imposing a citizenship share was not searched beyond the web searches. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register queries on contractor citizenship across agencies and for GSA, the FAR overhaul page, a congress.gov and GovInfo search of titles, the Justice Department newsroom, and one news search found no law, bill, executive order or rule requiring a citizenship share of contractor employees. Bill texts for contractor workforce bills were not opened and the Unified Agenda listing could not be browsed.
